SOURCE STORE IS THE EDIT TARGET: agent-system/extensions/core/** (never a deployed .claude/** tree, which is a gitignored, disposable deploy artifact regenerated from the source store -- see rules/source-store-deploy-boundary.md). Edit at the path mirroring the deployed one, then REDEPLOY via deploy-headless.sh. No task-number references and no record-versioning language in any file landing under agent-system/** (rules/no-task-references-in-deliverables.md, rules/no-record-versioning-in-deliverables.md); both are permitted in this description and elsewhere in specs/**.

ORIGIN: measured during an /orchestrate batch gate run. verify-deploy.sh's full gate set returned exit 1 with seven confirmed Gate 8 findings, all unattributable to any task in that batch (attributed={}, unattributed=7) -- pre-existing reds, not regressions the batch introduced. Six of those seven have since been closed (see ALREADY RESOLVED below, recorded as provenance so the work is neither re-derived nor silently dropped). One substantive defect remains, and it is the whole of this task's scope.

REMAINING SCOPE -- the .mcp.json merge defect (test-mcp-merge-target.sh):

test-mcp-merge-target.sh is the single remaining Gate 8 member that is a genuine defect. It fails two assertions that point at one underlying bug with a data-loss shape: a user's hand-authored .mcp.json server entry does not survive a load/regenerate cycle, and does not survive an unload.

- Assertion C (requirement d) reports hand-written='MISSING' fixture='stdio' where my-own-server / stdio was expected. The hand-written entry is being dropped where it must be preserved alongside the fixture's generated entry.
- Assertion E reports that the hand-written entry was disturbed by unload after a regenerate, when it must survive regardless of the retraction outcome.

Treat correctness of the merge as the default and the test expectations as correct unless evidence says otherwise. Preserve the existing additive-merge / tracked-removal contract -- the fix is to make the merge honor that contract, not to rewrite the contract to match current behavior. Diagnose whether C and E share one root cause or are two faults in the same code path, and say which in the summary.

GATE STATE: verify-deploy.sh currently reports FAIL -- 1 of 42 check(s) failed, down from 3. The single remaining failure is gate 8 (run-all.sh exit 1), whose surviving members are this mcp-merge defect plus the four pre-existing known-failures.txt rows.

ALREADY RESOLVED -- provenance only, not instructions. Do not re-diagnose these:

(1) test-lint-unit-integration-boundary.sh -- FIXED, now 15 passed / 0 failed (was 14/1). Two suites had no row in suite-classification.data (test-lint-fixture-dependency-declaration.sh, test-sapience-context-scoping.sh). Both classify unit, verified mechanically since neither invokes deploy-headless.sh, verify-deploy.sh or run-all.sh. Commit e1aedeaa7.

(2) test-runtime-file-tracking.sh -- FIXED, now 9/0 (was 8/1). A prose sweep in commit a3e7b5bd9 deleted the line **/.errors.lock from the fenced gitignore block in context/standards/orchestrator-runtime-files.md while scripts/lib/runtime-file-patterns.sh still emits it; the doc line was restored. Commits 2e76a8206, plus 5f1198e78 for the index-entries.json line_count reconcile.

(3) test-lint-hook-registration-paths.sh -- FIXED, now 32/0 (was 30/2). Two frozen exemplars (case21 SPSDemo, case23b theorem_proving_in_lean4) pinned the pre-widening Notification matcher permission_prompt|elicitation_dialog, stale since the matcher widened to permission_prompt|idle_prompt|elicitation_dialog. Both refreshed. Case20's fixture was deliberately NOT touched: it pins both matchers to reconstruct a historical cross-matcher drift. Commit 82a8c449e.

(4) test-deploy-baseline-lib.sh -- FIXED, now 30/0 (was 27/3). The vd_full_run_check helper hardcoded exactly 9 [PASS] lines from gate 1, but commit a0c070f42 deliberately narrowed that corpus from 9 files to 6 by removing errors-append.sh, errors-schema.json and errors-format.md. The count was updated to 6. Commit e1080bc3a.

(5) test-gate-lock.sh -- NOT A DEFECT. 27 passed / 0 failed on two separate direct runs. The batch gate's finding was almost certainly lock contention, not a real failure. The only open question -- whether the gate's own confirmation re-run should filter this -- is a gate-harness question, not a defect in this suite, and is not in scope here.

(6) test-gate-cache-equivalence.sh -- NOT A NEW DEFECT. Already rostered in scripts/tests/known-failures.txt as load-sensitive | needs-owner, with a hinted whole-suite cost of 543 seconds and a documented gate10-timeout interaction, triaged in specs/archive/170_isolate_shell_suites_from_host_state/reports/02_corpus-triage-ledger.md. The earlier 180-second probe was simply too short a timeout, not evidence of failure. Read that known-failures row and that ledger before spending any dispatch on this suite.

BINDING CONSTRAINTS:
- Do not silence a failure by deleting, skipping, or loosening an assertion to make it pass. If a suite's expectation is genuinely wrong, correct it and state in the plan why the new expectation is right.
- Do not add any suite to known-failures.txt as the remedy. That roster exists for deliberately-expected reds; using it here would convert a fixable defect into a permanent exemption.
- Do not expand scope into the adjacent open work on the same directory: the known-failures roster for test-deploy-propagation.sh and its sibling, and the orchestrator's stall-on-backgrounded-verify-deploy behavior, are separately tracked and are not part of this task.

ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA:
1. bash .claude/scripts/verify-deploy.sh completes its full gate set with exit 0.
2. test-mcp-merge-target.sh passes on a direct run, with its pass/fail counts quoted verbatim in the summary.
3. The summary names which side was wrong -- the merge code or the test's own expectation -- and why.
4. The known-failures.txt entry count is unchanged or lower, never higher.
5. deploy-headless.sh reports RESULT=landed_verify_clean.
